title: Atomic Econ Lens — Field Notes & Sketchbook
content:
Purpose: quick field-notes for the "atomic econ" lens: a lightweight, investigatory view that helps engineers and product owners understand per-invocation economics at token granularity without overwhelming them. This doc is intentionally rough — sketches, heuristics, backlog candidates and edge-case scenarios. Keep it pragmatic: measurable, actionable, and instrumentable by infra/runtime teams.

Why this exists
- Problem: customers and internal teams need to debug sudden spikes in per-invocation cost and tail latency. Existing dashboards surface aggregate averages but not how specific token paths, prompt prefixes, or streaming patterns drive cost.
- Goal: give a compact, drillable surface that maps from invocation -> token timeline -> cost/latency attribution -> suggested mitigations.

Personas
- Platform SRE: triages latency regressions during incidents. Needs fast filters and ability to pin a problematic invocation.
- ML infra engineer: wants to understand KV-cache hit patterns, prefix reuse, batching efficiency. Needs raw per-token metrics and traces.
- Product manager / Solutions Eng: wants a clear narrative to explain cost anomalies to customers and recommend configuration changes.

High-level UX principles
- Start collapsed: show summary line per invocation (total tokens, total cost, p50/p95 latency). Expand to token timeline only on demand.
- Progressive reveal: default to sampled traces (1-in-N) for heavy workloads; allow full-trace for selected invocations.
- Actionable suggestions: surface 2–3 automated heuristics per suspicious invocation (e.g., recommend smaller max_new_tokens, enable prefix caching, quantized variant suggestion).
- Preserve privacy: token content must be masked by default (shows token length + type). Clear control to unmask for customer-owned data if allowed.

Core view (wireframe A — compact inspector)
- Left column: filter bar (time range, model family, region, customer-tier, route, has-embeddings, sampling rate). Quick toggles: show only high-cost, show only p95 regressed, show anomalous token growth.
- Middle: invocation list (each row = invocation snapshot). Row elements: timestamp, route, model, total tokens, total cost, total latency, small sparkline for token emission rate (tokens/sec). Each row has expand chevron.
- Right (when expanded): token timeline waterfall. Horizontal x-axis = time (ms), vertical bands = token buckets grouped by source (prompt, system, tool, user, model-generated). Each token drawn as a thin column with height mapped to token compute cost (relative) and color mapped to latency source (red=attention, orange=io wait, blue=kv fetch, green=compute). Hovering a token shows: token-index, token-source, token-length, cost (micro-units), latency breakdown (kernel, memcpy, scheduling).
- Inline micro-actions: pin invocation, flag as regression, open in replay player, request full trace (async job).

Sketch notes (interaction details)
- Hover expansion should be near-instant; heavy traces should load progressively (first show aggregated bucket bars, then stream token columns).
- Allow selection of contiguous token ranges to compute delta-cost and delta-latency (useful to see how a prompt prefix caused elevated cost). Selection summary shows recommended mitigations and an estimated cost-savings if mitigated.
- Provide a token-slice comparator: choose two invocations and show overlayed timelines and a per-token delta heatmap.

Data model / what we need from runtime (minimal viable telemetry)
- Invocation meta: id, route, model, region, start_ts, end_ts, total_tokens, config(max_new_tokens, temp, sampling/streaming flags).
- Token series (sampled or full): index, time_offset_ms, source_tag, token_length_bytes, kv_cache_hit(bool), compute_cycles_estimate, kernel_time_ms, io_time_ms.
- Derived: token_cost_estimate (raw), cumulative_cost, pX latency windows.
- Trace retention: default 14 days for full traces; aggregate rollups retained 90 days. Provide on-demand longer retention per-account.

Heuristics & automated suggestions (playbook snippets)
- Heuristic: long-prefix-repeat — if >20% of tokens match prior invocation prefixes and per-token cost spikes, suggest enabling prefix_cache for route and show estimated savings.
- Heuristic: burst-emission — if tokens/sec > threshold and p95 latency regressed, recommend increased batching window or smaller beam width.
- Heuristic: kv-starvation — frequent kernel io time tied to model-variant suggests quantization variant or larger KV partition.
- Each heuristic has: detection rule (SQL-ish pseudo), confidence score, expected savings, recommended config change, ticket link template to run rollout.

Privacy & compliance notes
- Default masking policy: redact token text for tenants in shared mode. Masking toggle requires an audit log and owner consent. Provide scrubbed examples (show token-length, token-type).
- PII detection: if detected, automatically anonymize and attach redaction note.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs
- Sampling strategy: fixed 1-in-100 vs adaptive sampling that increases when anomaly detectors fire. Tradeoff: complexity vs cost.
- How much kernel-level detail can SLO metrics surface without leaking infra internals? Need SRE/security review.
- Should we offload full-trace storage to dedicated S3 buckets per customer to meet retention/compliance? Ops feasibility?

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Can filter invocations by route/model/time and view per-invocation summary.
- Expand an invocation to see token buckets and hover metric breakdown (token index, cost, latency components).
- Show at least two heuristics with suggested actions and link-to-rollout template.
- Sampling toggle and request-full-trace flow exists (async job).

Backlog & next steps (prioritized)
- P0: build invocation list + expand to basic token-bucket waterline (skeleton view, sampled tokens) — owner: eng-console, estimate: 2 sprints.
- P1: implement heuristic engine (start with prefix-repeat and burst-emission) + UI hooks — owner: infra/telemetry + product.
- P1: add masking toggle + audit log + consent flow — owner: security/compliance.
- P2: comparator view (side-by-side invocation compare) and delta-heatmap — owner: ux + frontend.
- P2: integrate cost-saving recommendations into rollout templates + auto-create JIRA — owner: product-ops.
- Long-term: live replay player (stream token playback), on-device/offline viewer for private deployments.

Quick wireframe annotations (for designers)
- Token colors should be semantic and consistent across product (attention/kv/io/compute). Include legend and ability to toggle color mapping.
- Provide a compact export: snapshot of invocation with suggested changes and estimated savings that can be attached to support tickets.
- Mobile: provide simplified list + compact sparkline only; expanded token timeline is desktop-only.

Notes for devs (implementation quirks)
- Start with a thin API: /insights/invocations?filters=... returns summaries. /insights/invocation/{id}/tokens?samples=100 returns sampled token series. Full trace job enqueues to /insights/trace-requests with callback URL.
- Use incremental loading to avoid jank. First payload: buckets group-by source (prompt/system/model) with counts and coarse costs. Second payload: sampled token items in time order.

Final thoughts / low-level heuristics to try experimentally
- Use entropy of token stream as a cheap anomaly detector — sudden drop in entropy often correlates with repetition loops that blow up token count.
- Track per-route prefix-reuse ratio over rolling 24h — routes with high reuse are good candidates for cache pins.

Immediate asks for this doc:
- Design: quick mockups for compact inspector + expanded timeline (Aisha).
- Infra: feasibility on storing token series at 1000 traces/day for large customers (Diego).
- Product: pick 2 beta customers and prepare a playbook for rollout and opt-in (Liam).

Appendix: rough sketch index references (hand-drawn)
- sketch-01: compact-list-with-timeline (attach later)
- sketch-02: token-slice-selector + suggestion panel
- sketch-03: comparator-layered-heatmap

End of notes — Marcus
